topic: PSA civil-registration funding and organizational capacity
summary: The bill sponsor sought funding for a modernized civil registration system, including digitization, expanded access, and anti-fraud safeguards. The PSA supported the bill and said the existing civil-registration law dated to 1931, but requested a stronger civil registration office under Section 6. It said the PSA and local civil registrars lacked sufficient capacity to expand registration services and protect records from fraud. The DBM answered that any office creation or strengthening would require its usual evaluation and review under the government optimization program. It also recommended using "existing retirement laws" and clarified that the legal service in Section 61 referred to the PSA's existing legal service. The organizational and funding issues remained open.
question: The committee was considering whether the substitute bill and its funding should provide for a stronger Philippine Civil Registry Office within the PSA, given the need to expand services and protect records from fraud. It also sought to establish how the proposed organizational changes would be evaluated by the DBM and how the bill's legal-service provision should be interpreted.
agency_position: The PSA supported the substitute bill but maintained that the civil registration office and the capacities of the PSA and local civil registrars needed to be strengthened to expand access and combat fraud. The DBM did not reject the organizational provision but said any creation or strengthening must undergo DBM evaluation and the government optimization program, and it requested clarification of the retirement-law and legal-service language.
outcome: The PSA's request for a stronger civil registration office and greater organizational capacity was placed on the record, but the DBM said the proposal remained subject to its evaluation and the government optimization program. DBM also placed proposed drafting clarifications on the record; no final decision on the requested strengthening or funding was stated.

positions.position: Supported immediate approval of the substitute bill and sought the necessary funding to implement the modernization of civil registration.

topic: 10% PSA registration-income retention for immediate operations
summary: Rep. Monique Lagdameo initially moved to delete the Section 78 provision concerning PSA-generated income. Rep. Rufus Rodriguez objected, arguing that PSA should retain 10% of registration income for immediate operations and modernization instead of waiting for congressional appropriations. DBM said it preferred the one-fund concept but deferred to the committee, warning that retention would reduce money entering the General Fund. The PSA-side author subsequently supported retaining the provision, while Rep. Romeo Momo cautioned that other earning agencies might seek similar treatment. The agency estimated the 10% at about 1.139 billion based on 2025 revenue. Lagdameo revised the motion to exclude the Section 78 deletion, and the chair approved it without objection.
question: The committee sought to determine whether Section 78 should retain a provision allowing the PSA to use 10% of civil-registration income for immediate operations and modernization, rather than placing all such income in the General Fund. Members also asked how much the retained income would yield.
agency_position: The DBM official maintained that DBM preferred the one-fund concept because it would provide flexibility during budget preparation and would preserve more resources for the General Fund. However, DBM deferred to the committee's decision on allowing PSA to retain 10% of generated income and did not object on the record to the committee's approval.
outcome: The committee approved the revised motion excluding the proposed deletion of Section 78, so the 10% PSA income-retention provision was retained. The agency estimated the 10% at 1,139,000,000 based on 2025 revenue, while the broader policy concern about setting a precedent for other earning agencies was left as a caution rather than resolved.

topic: Infrastructure master plan council size and agency overlap
summary: Romeo Momo Jr. sponsored a thirty-year infrastructure master plan and a presidentially chaired MIND Council. DEPDEV argued that the CIDMP and council substantially overlapped with functions already assigned to DEPDEV and related bodies under Republic Act number 12145, while DBM addressed staffing and appropriations language. Rep. Rodriguez questioned the proposed council of 28 members and suggested reducing it to about 11, with Rep. Pomerangay supporting agency participation only as needed. Romeo Momo Jr. said the broad membership was intended to prevent conflicts among infrastructure plans and agreed to review the membership issue. The committee ultimately adopted amendments requiring use of DEPDEV's existing staffing complement, DBM evaluation and approval of designations, and more general appropriations language, then approved the measure subject to those amendments.
question: The committee sought to establish whether the proposed master plan and MIND Council duplicated existing DEPDEV functions, and whether the council's proposed membership was workable. It also considered how the council secretariat would be staffed and whether DBM approval would be required.
agency_position: DEPDEV said the CIDMP and MIND Council substantially overlapped with functions already assigned to DEPDEV, the ED Council, and the Infrastructure Development Committee under Republic Act number 12145, and recommended strengthening existing structures instead of creating parallel ones. DBM supported use of DEPDEV's existing staffing complement and required DBM evaluation and approval for any designation or creation of positions, while favoring more flexible appropriations language.
outcome: The committee adopted amendments addressing staffing, DBM oversight, and appropriations wording, then approved the measure subject to those amendments. The broader dispute over whether the MIND Council duplicated DEPDEV and whether its membership should be reduced was discussed, but no specific reduction in council membership was adopted in the recorded proceedings.

topic: Disaster risk financing, DREAM Funds, and insurance structure
summary: Rep. Joseph Lara sponsored the DRFI framework, citing annual disaster-related asset losses of about 177 billion and an equivalent of about US3.5 billion dollars. OCD supported the measure but asked that its relationship with the existing DREAM Funds be clearly defined and protected against duplication. DOF supported prearranged financing, multilayered risk financing, and parametric insurance, while the Insurance Commission sought clearer boundaries over government assets, existing institutions, asset prioritization, and claims guidelines. Treasury objected to creating a special fund because of the regular budget process, trust-receipt treatment of insurance proceeds, and the one-fund policy. DBM recommended calling it a program funded through a GAA line item and requiring DBM review of positions. The committee adopted those amendments and approved the measure, although a member's parametric-insurance clarification received a garbled and unclear response.
question: The committee was trying to establish how the proposed disaster risk financing and insurance framework would complement existing DREAM Funds and government insurance arrangements, and whether the proposed financing mechanism should be a special fund or a program. It also sought to clarify the respective roles of the Insurance Commission, Department of Finance, Bureau of the Treasury, DBM, and the proposed DRFIB.
agency_position: The agencies supported the DRFI substitute bill but sought clearer boundaries and implementation rules. OCD supported the framework as complementary to the DREAM Funds; DOF supported prearranged financing and parametric insurance; the Insurance Commission requested clarification of coverage and government-insurance responsibilities; Treasury opposed creating a special fund under the one-fund policy; and DBM recommended treating the mechanism as a program funded through a GAA line item.
outcome: The committee adopted the agency-backed amendments, converting the proposed DRFI special fund into a program, subjecting implementation to DBM guidelines, and requiring DBM evaluation and approval of positions. It then approved the DRFI measure subject to those amendments; the precise response to the parametric-insurance clarification was left unclear in the transcript.

topic: Community Driven Development appropriations and implementation safeguards
summary: Rep. France Pomeran sponsored the substitute bill institutionalizing CDD and described its community-participation, transparency, accountability, and poverty-reduction objectives. DSWD supported the measure without objection, including the appropriations provision and the inclusion of amounts necessary for continued implementation in the annual General Appropriations Act. DBM requested flexible language referring to prevailing community-participation procurement guidelines and fiscal safeguards for agreements with LGUs. The committee adopted both amendments and approved the measure subject to them. No specific peso amount was stated; the appropriations commitment was described as current agency appropriations and amounts as may be necessary for continued implementation.
question: The committee was determining whether to institutionalize Community Driven Development (CDD) as a national strategy, provide appropriations for its sustained implementation, and establish safeguards for participation, procurement, LGU agreements, accounting, and auditing. It also considered whether the proposed implementation provisions required technical amendments.
agency_position: DSWD supported the substitute bill, had no objection to it, and supported the appropriations provision for sustained implementation subject to applicable budgeting, accounting, and auditing requirements. DBM supported clarifying the bill so procurement would follow prevailing community-participation guidelines and LGU agreements would remain subject to existing fiscal-control laws and regulations.
outcome: The committee approved the CDD institutionalization measure subject to amendments. The amendments incorporated flexible, prevailing procurement guidance and explicit compliance with existing budgeting, accounting, and auditing requirements for LGU agreements.

thread.speaker: Rep. France Pomeran
thread.said: Rep. Pomeran said poverty reduction and inclusive development could not be sustained by government intervention alone. He described CDD as treating communities as development partners and involving them in identifying needs, planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation.

thread.speaker: Rep. France Pomeran
thread.said: He said the substitute bill would require national government agencies and local government units to adopt CDD in community-based programs benefiting poor, vulnerable, disadvantaged, and marginalized communities. The measure emphasized participation, transparency, accountability, and local ownership.

thread.speaker: Rep. France Pomeran
thread.said: He identified the proposed National Program on Community Driven Development as providing capacity building, technical assistance, social accountability mechanisms, and linkages between community priorities and local and national development programs.

thread.speaker: Rep. France Pomeran
thread.said: He said the measure would give particular consideration to Indigenous Peoples and other marginalized sectors and would enable communities to participate in disaster preparedness, risk reduction, and resilience-building.

thread.speaker: Rep. France Pomeran
thread.said: He said the bill contained financial-management, monitoring, reporting, and grievance mechanisms to ensure that resources for community development were properly managed and implementation remained transparent and accountable. He characterized the measure as a framework for existing government programs rather than another layer of bureaucracy.

thread.speaker: Rep. France Pomeran
thread.said: Rep. Pomeran asked for favorable consideration and expeditious passage of the measure, saying poverty reduction would be more sustainable when communities participated in shaping and implementing their own development. He formally sponsored the numbered substitute House bill.

thread.speaker: DSWD deputy national program official Didit Boson
thread.said: On behalf of the DSWD, the official expressed support and no objection to the substitute bill. DSWD welcomed the appropriations provision and said the bill adopted current appropriations of the DSWD and other concerned agencies, subject to applicable budgeting, accounting, and auditing laws, rules, and regulations.

thread.speaker: DSWD deputy national program official Didit Boson
thread.said: DSWD supported including appropriate amounts as may be necessary for continued implementation of the program in the annual General Appropriations Act. It also reaffirmed its commitment to work with Congress, government agencies, LGUs, civil society organizations, and communities on a sustainable, inclusive, participatory, gender-responsive, and climate-resilient CDD framework.

thread.speaker: DBM Andrea Celine Magtalas
thread.said: DBM proposed revising the reference in Section 14 so the provision would refer to the prevailing guidelines for the conduct of community participation in procurement, rather than a specific set of revised guidelines. DBM said this would preserve flexibility as guidelines changed.

thread.speaker: DBM Andrea Celine Magtalas
thread.said: For Section 15, DBM proposed clarifying that an implementing agency's option to enter into a memorandum of agreement with concerned LGUs would remain subject to existing budgeting, auditing, and accounting laws, rules, and regulations.

thread.speaker: Monique Lagdameo
thread.said: The vice chair presented the committee's suggested amendments. For Section 14, the committee would insert the word "prevailing" and language referring to guidelines "for the conduct" of community participation.

thread.speaker: Monique Lagdameo
thread.said: For Section 15, the vice chair proposed inserting the phrase "subject to existing budgeting, accounting, and auditing laws, rules, and regulations."

thread.speaker: Chair
thread.said: The chair asked for the sponsor's position. Rep. Pomeran accepted the amendments, and the chair declared the motion to approve the amendments approved after a second and no objection.

thread.speaker: Monique Lagdameo
thread.said: The vice chair moved to approve the measure subject to the stated amendments.

thread.speaker: Chair
thread.said: The chair reported that the motion had been seconded and, with no objection, declared the measure approved subject to the amendments.

topic: Medical education infrastructure and CHED funding
summary: The bill sponsor and an author presented the proposed Philippine Medical Act as a modernization measure covering medical education, internship, postgraduate training, and physician regulation. PRC supported the bill and noted the proposed increase in PRB membership from six to seven and terms from three years to five years. PRC nevertheless questioned the creation and budget of the PGMEC and proposed adapting the existing CPSP program instead. CHED supported the bill but requested financial support for subsidiary bodies, an organic secretariat, data infrastructure, fee utilization, and state universities and colleges. PRC committed to submit its position, but the transcript recorded no final resolution on the funding or PGMEC issues.
question: The committee was seeking to establish how the proposed Philippine Medical Act would affect medical education, postgraduate training, regulatory councils, and the budgets of PRC and CHED. It also sought the agencies' positions on the proposed postgraduate medical education committee and the financial and infrastructure requirements of the new functions.
agency_position: PRC and the Board of Medicine fully supported the substitute bill but expressed reservations about the PGMEC, citing budget differences and proposing use of the existing CPSP program instead. CHED also fully supported the bill but asked that its new regulatory responsibilities be matched with funding for subsidiary bodies, an organic secretariat, data infrastructure, fee utilization, and support for state universities and colleges.
outcome: The agencies supported the bill but identified unresolved funding and institutional-design issues. PRC undertook to submit its position on the PGMEC, while CHED recommended budget and infrastructure adjustments; no final funding decision was recorded.

positions.position: Supported the bill as necessary to modernize medical education, internship, postgraduate training, and physician regulation.
Supported passage of the bill to update medical education and training and integrate the full medical-profession framework.

thread.speaker: Jun Gato, bill sponsor
thread.said: The sponsor said the measure would modernize the law governing the licensure and registration of physicians and standardize, regulate, and upgrade basic medical education, medical internship, and postgraduate medical training.

thread.speaker: Giselle Maseda, bill author
thread.said: Maseda supported passage of the bill, saying it would update medical education and training, foster continuing professional development, and integrate medical education, internship, residency training, licensure, registration, and practice into one framework.

thread.speaker: Sheila Halbuena, CHED Office of Programs and Standards Development

thread.speaker: Sheila Halbuena, CHED Office of Programs and Standards Development

thread.speaker: Sheila Halbuena, CHED Office of Programs and Standards Development

topic: Resident and fellow compensation and DBM salary review
summary: The DOH supported improving resident and fellow compensation but requested further study and a budgetary impact analysis. It identified the current entry-level resident classification as salary grade 21 and the proposed classification as salary grade 22. DBM warned that a fixed salary grade 22 minimum could distort hospital employee salaries and proposed using the revised compensation and position classification system, subject to DBM review and applicable rules. The sponsors accepted the DBM recommendations, including safeguards for the medical councils and budgeting, accounting, and auditing provisions. The committee approved the amendments and then approved the measure subject to those amendments, while the requested budgetary impact study remained unaddressed as a separate action.
question: The committee was determining how the proposed compensation increase for residents and fellows should be evaluated, including its budgetary impact and compatibility with the government compensation system. It also considered DBM safeguards for the creation of medical councils and provisions affecting foreign medical graduates.
agency_position: The DOH supported improving resident and fellow compensation, including review of the current salary classification, but called for further studies and a budgetary impact analysis. DBM opposed prescribing a fixed salary grade 22 floor because of possible salary distortions and instead sought application of the revised compensation and position classification system, subject to DBM evaluation and approval and applicable laws and regulations.
outcome: The committee removed the fixed salary grade 22 floor and adopted DBM's revised compensation and position classification approach, subject to DBM evaluation and approval. The amendments and the Philippine Medical Act measure were approved without objection; the DOH's requested budgetary impact study was not separately resolved in the transcript.

topic: Local-government performance incentives and SGLG funding
summary: Rep. Albert Garcia sponsored a bill establishing a data-driven performance-measurement system for local governments and linking improvements to performance-based rewards. He cited a system covering about 42,000 barangayes, 1,400-plus local-government units, about 180 cities, and 82 provinces. DBM recommended removing national government agencies from the scope, requiring DBM approval for additional positions, coordinating with DILG on barangay bonuses, retaining the SGLG fund, and preserving the 2% operating-fund provision. Garcia accepted the DBM comments, and the committee adopted corresponding amendments, including retention of SGLG provisions and deletion of references to national government agencies. The committee approved the amendments and the measure, subject to style.
question: The committee was determining how the proposed performance-measurement and meritocracy system would apply to local governments and barangays, including the treatment of national government agencies. It also examined whether the Seal of Good Local Governance (SGLG) fund, barangay performance-based bonuses, DBM approval requirements, and the 2% operating-fund cap should be retained or amended.
agency_position: DBM supported adjusting the bill to remove national government agencies from its scope while retaining DBM approval for additional positions, coordinating with DILG on barangay performance bonuses, and preserving and harmonizing the SGLG fund provisions. DBM also supported retaining the 2% SGLG-fund operating provision, subject to drafting harmonization and style.
outcome: The committee approved the amendments and then approved the measure subject to those amendments and style. The approved package removed national government agencies, retained the SGLG fund provisions, preserved the 2% phrase, and added DBM approval and DILG-DBM coordination requirements.

positions.position: Supported the performance-measurement and meritocracy bill and accepted DBM's comments and all committee amendments, including removal of national government agencies, retention of SGLG provisions, and retention of the 2% SGLG-fund phrase.

thread.speaker: Rep. Albert Garcia
thread.said: Rep. Garcia sponsored an unnumbered substitute bill establishing a performance-measurement system to promote meritocracy in government and amending Republic Act No. 11292, the Seal of Good Local Governance Act of 2019.

thread.speaker: Rep. Albert Garcia
thread.said: He said the measure would elevate the SGLG criteria while retaining bottom-line conditions and checklists based on data and measurable outcomes.

thread.speaker: Rep. Albert Garcia
thread.said: He identified health, education, per capita income, peace and order, and affordability as pillars, and said the system would distribute responsibility for the national vision among local governments.

thread.speaker: Rep. Albert Garcia
thread.said: He referred to 42,000 plus barangayes, 1,400 plus municipalities, cities, 180 or so cities, and 82 provinces as participating local-government units.

thread.speaker: Rep. Albert Garcia
thread.said: He said local governments would be rewarded based on performance rather than receiving national-government assistance or support on a dole-out basis, which he said would professionalize public service and improve quality of life.
